A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same depth-scaling study of contrastive reinforcement learning. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated goal-reaching experiments, depth-scaling results, architectural ablations, stitching tests, and simulator-version comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, controlled learning experiments, architectural analyses, offline evaluations, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The main InfoNCE-based CRL method and residual-block architecture remain unchanged. v3 adds subsidiary procedural adaptations: CMD-1 with backward NCE and MRN representations in Appendix A.4, and hyperspherical weight normalization after gradient updates in A.6. These extend the scaling recipe without replacing its central method.

E1.justification: The ten online JaxGCRL tasks and offline CRL evaluation on OGBench remain. Appendix A.3 adds online QRL on FetchPush and expert-SAC-data behavioral cloning on antmaze-giant-navigate, extending the tested scenarios within simulated control. Newly specifying previously unnamed OGBench tasks does not itself establish additional coverage.

E2.justification: v1 primarily compares CRL architectures and depths. v3 Appendix A.1 adds actual comparisons against SAC, SAC+HER, TD3+HER, GCSL, and GCBC across the ten environments; A.2 also compares their depth-scaling behavior. This substantially expands the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 introduces shared-replay controls using depth-4 or depth-32 collectors and non-collecting learners, plus runtime-to-performance evaluation against SAC. Its reported width comparison includes widths through 2048 rather than v1's 4096. The original 1000-step time-at-goal metric and last-five-epochs averaging remain; these additions do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds exploration-versus-capacity controls, trajectory-embedding analysis, LayerNorm and activation ablations, residual-activation measurements, and scaling studies involving other algorithms and normalization schemes. These address substantial new mechanistic and applicability questions. Existing stitching, actor-versus-critic, residual-connection, and simulator-version analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use ± entries, shaded curves, and error bars without specifying run counts, seeds, or what the uncertainty marks represent. v3 extends these displays to additional results but does not document a changed statistical reporting or estimation practice.

E6.justification: Figure 1 and Table 1 retain the original results, including Humanoid scores of 12.6 ± 1.3 and 649 ± 19 at depths 4 and 64. v3 adds baseline rankings, architectural and mechanistic outcomes, and runtime results. Its offline results also qualify v1's blanket negative account by reporting improvement on antmaze-medium-stitch. These are additional or revised findings, not gains in the retained headline results.

T1.justification: The goal-conditioned MDP definitions, discounted-visitation/value relationship, CRL objectives, and residual recursion are retained. The added quasimetric motivation does not introduce a new formal derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly claim superiority over other goal-conditioned baselines, developed into a state-of-the-art claim in Section 4.2. The central claims about scaling to 1024 layers, large improvements over shallow CRL, and qualitatively different learned behaviors remain.

C2.justification: v1 tentatively links depth's benefits to exploration. v3 develops a substantive account involving jointly improved exploration and expressivity, and proposes that deeper networks allocate more representational capacity near goals. It also discusses algorithm-dependent scalability, qualifies the offline limitation, and distinguishes higher total training cost from favorable time to reach a performance target.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3–B.4 adds substantial resource documentation: training times across environments and depths through 1024, baseline runtimes, and time to surpass SAC's final performance. The code address and most hyperparameters remain unchanged, while Table 7 omits v1's action_repeat=1 entry. Hardware details remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Chang et al. on residual networks and Liu et al. and Wang et al. on metric/quasimetric learning, plus discussion of Simba-v2 compatibility. The main related-work narrative and positioning around self-supervision, classification objectives, and depth versus width remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: several separate v1 subsections are regrouped under What Matters for CRL Scaling and Why Scaling Happens. Appendices are reorganized, captions are condensed, and the conclusion's boxed findings summary is removed while its substantive findings remain elsewhere.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main document from two columns to one, redraws the width comparison against parameter count, rearranges batch-size panels, and moves Table 1 and the environment montage into the appendix. Numerous comparison, analysis, and runtime displays are added. Two different figures are labeled Figure 12, introducing cross-reference ambiguity.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens two weak points in v1: competitive validation beyond CRL variants and controlled evidence about why depth helps. The added baseline comparisons, shared-replay experiment, component ablations, offline exceptions, and runtime measurements make the empirical case and its boundaries more assessable. Sparse statistical and hardware reporting and duplicate figure numbering limit clarity, but the substantive evidential gains outweigh these shortcomings.
